landscape.label: 2026 Price Guide
title: Kitchen Remodel
Pricing Guide
landscape.say: How much does a kitchen remodel cost in Santa Clarita in 2026? Most remodelers won't give you a number until they've been in your house for an hour. Here's the pricing guide, with real published prices.

landscape.label: 2026 Price Tiers
landscape.title: What a Santa Clarita kitchen remodel costs
landscape.sub: 2026 ranges · most projects land in one of three
landscape.say: Most Santa Clarita kitchen projects land in one of three ranges. An entry-level remodel starts at about $25,000 to $35,000. A mid-range remodel, the most popular, typically runs $40,000 to $70,000. And a high-end remodel runs $75,000 to $120,000 and up.
landscape.speak: Most Santa Clarita kitchen projects land in one of three ranges. An entry-level remodel starts at about twenty-five thousand dollars to thirty-five thousand dollars. A mid-range remodel, the most popular, typically runs forty thousand dollars to seventy thousand dollars. And a high-end remodel runs seventy-five thousand dollars to one hundred twenty thousand dollars and up.

landscape.label: Tier 1 of 3
landscape.name: Entry-level remodel

bullets.t: Cabinet refacing or new stock cabinets

landscape.say: An entry-level remodel, at $25,000 to $35,000, is for quick refreshes, rentals, and first-time buyers. You keep the existing layout and appliances, with cabinet refacing or new stock cabinets, laminate or quartz countertops, and new lighting, backsplash, paint, and flooring.
landscape.speak: An entry-level remodel, at twenty-five thousand dollars to thirty-five thousand dollars, is for quick refreshes, rentals, and first-time buyers. You keep the existing layout and appliances, with cabinet refacing or new stock cabinets, laminate or quartz countertops, and new lighting, backsplash, paint, and flooring.

landscape.label: Tier 2 of 3
landscape.name: Mid-range remodel
landscape.desc: The full upgrade most Santa Clarita families choose.

bullets.t: Quartz, granite or butcher block counters
Updated layout, sink, faucet & tile backsplash

landscape.say: A mid-range remodel, $40,000 to $70,000, is the full upgrade most Santa Clarita families choose: new semi-custom cabinets, quartz, granite, or butcher block counters, an updated layout with a new sink, faucet, and tile backsplash, and plumbing or electrical relocations.
landscape.speak: A mid-range remodel, forty thousand dollars to seventy thousand dollars, is the full upgrade most Santa Clarita families choose: new semi-custom cabinets, quartz, granite, or butcher block counters, an updated layout with a new sink, faucet, and tile backsplash, and plumbing or electrical relocations.

landscape.label: Tier 3 of 3
landscape.name: High-end remodel
landscape.say: A high-end remodel, $75,000 to $120,000 and up, is a custom, chef-grade kitchen: a layout redesign and wall reconfiguration, custom cabinetry with built-in organizers, full-slab quartz or granite, commercial-grade appliances, and a custom island or built-in seating.
landscape.speak: A high-end remodel, seventy-five thousand dollars to one hundred twenty thousand dollars and up, is a custom, chef-grade kitchen: a layout redesign and wall reconfiguration, custom cabinetry with built-in organizers, full-slab quartz or granite, commercial-grade appliances, and a custom island or built-in seating.

landscape.label: Permit Costs
landscape.title: Typical permit costs (2026)
landscape.note: Set by the city and based on your project's valuation. Shown as its own line on your quote.
landscape.say: Budget for permits too. They typically run $500 to $1,500. A minor remodel with no layout changes, about $400 to $700. Removing walls or upgrading plumbing or electrical, about $800 to $1,200. And major structural changes, $1,200 to $1,500 and up. The fee is set by the city, based on your project's value.
landscape.speak: Budget for permits too. They typically run five hundred dollars to fifteen hundred dollars. A minor remodel with no layout changes, about four hundred dollars to seven hundred dollars. Removing walls or upgrading plumbing or electrical, about eight hundred dollars to twelve hundred dollars. And major structural changes, twelve hundred dollars to fifteen hundred dollars and up. The fee is set by the city, based on your project's value.

landscape.label: What Drives the Price
landscape.title: What moves your price

cards.name: Layout changes
cards.desc: Keeping the sink, range & fridge in place saves the most

cards.name: Cabinets
cards.desc: Refacing or stock vs. semi-custom or custom

cards.name: Countertops
cards.desc: Laminate & quartz vs. full slab or waterfall

cards.name: Appliances
cards.desc: Reusing saves thousands; commercial ranges need venting

landscape.say: Two kitchens the same size can come in $30,000 apart. What makes the difference? Layout changes: keeping your sink, range, and fridge where they are is the single biggest way to save. Then cabinets, countertops, and appliances, where reusing what you have saves thousands.
landscape.speak: Two kitchens the same size can come in thirty thousand dollars apart. What makes the difference? Layout changes: keeping your sink, range, and fridge where they are is the single biggest way to save. Then cabinets, countertops, and appliances, where reusing what you have saves thousands.

landscape.label: Optional Upgrades
landscape.title: Upgrades that add cost
items: Pot fillers, second sinks & beverage stations
landscape.note: None are required for a beautiful kitchen. Price them separately and decide.
landscape.say: Optional upgrades add to the total: panel-ready appliances, radiant heated floors, skylights or bigger windows, pot fillers and beverage stations, smart lighting, and walk-in pantries or custom storage. None of them are required for a beautiful kitchen.
